headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from a memory agent feeding a local trainer; no direct data-exfil path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee can ingest documents, workflows, and support history, while LlamaFactory is a training/instruction-tuning system with no documented provenance filter. If cognee outputs are copied into training or prompts, malicious content can steer downstream behavior. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly evidenced, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF cognee outputs are manually copied into LlamaFactory training data or prompts
IF LlamaFactory is used to fine-tune on untrusted support documents without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a 5-minute review step before any cognee export is reused
Tag imported text as untrusted in the training pipeline
Strip instructions from support documents before fine-tuning
Use a separate staging dataset for one test run
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between the tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal and finance data, but LlamaFactory has network egress none and no filesystem or clipboard surfaces, so there is no documented path for it to transmit data. The main risk is local exposure if operators manually move sensitive exports between them; that is a narrow, non-default pathway.
conditions: IF an operator manually exports sensitive cognee data into LlamaFactory training files
IF those exports are stored on a shared workstation without access controls
mitigations: Keep sensitive exports out of training sets
Use a redacted sample dataset for quick tests
Delete temporary export files after use
Restrict local file permissions on the export folder
requires-engineering: separate sensitive-memory storage from training inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee has allowlisted network egress and session memory, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem write, no shell, no subprocesses, and no network egress. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF a separate orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF external tooling adds shared mutable state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant extra filesystem or git permissions
Verify the orchestrator does not add hidden shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which LlamaFactory could treat as training or instruction data. If those outputs are reused without verification, errors or hallucinations can be amplified into future models or prompts. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory ingests cognee-generated decisions as authoritative labels
IF no human verification occurs before reuse in fine-tuning or prompt templates
mitigations: Require human review of cognee outputs before reuse
Keep a gold-label validation set separate from generated data
Sample-check a few reused records each run
Document which fields are machine-generated
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while LlamaFactory has no stated compliance controls, residency, or retention policy. If regulated support data is moved into LlamaFactory workflows, the mismatch can create a compliance gap. Because only one agent shows regulated data handling, the other is cited for missing controls rather than a specific jurisdictional claim.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data from cognee is exported into LlamaFactory training or logs
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to that exported data
mitigations: Avoid exporting regulated data into training artifacts
Use anonymized or synthetic samples
Set a short manual retention window for exports
Record a deletion checklist for each run
requires-engineering: define a compliance boundary and retention policy
